title: Dune (1991 demo)
author: Cryo, for Virgin Games
blurb: The playable demo of Cryo's Dune: the Virgin and Cryo logos, then Arrakis, with Stéphane Picq's AdLib music.

title: Unreal
author: Future Crew
blurb: Future Crew's demo from Assembly '92, with its Sound Blaster music: the menu is set to SoundBlaster Pro (left arrow, then Enter).

title: DOOM (shareware)
author: id Software
blurb: Episode one, Knee-Deep in the Dead, from id's own 1.9 shareware archive. It runs on MIRAGE's DPMI host, with its music and sound effects on the Sound Blaster (a DEFAULT.CFG of ours sets it up; the sound starts with your first click or key).

title: Heretic (shareware)
author: Raven Software, published by id Software
blurb: The first episode of Raven's fantasy DOOM, from the 1.2 shareware archive. It runs on MIRAGE's DPMI host, with its music and sound effects on the Sound Blaster (a HERETIC.CFG of ours sets it up; the sound starts with your first click or key).

title: C-Dogs 1.06
author: Ronny Wester
blurb: Ronny Wester's top-down shooter for one or two players, the sequel to Cyberdogs, on DOS/4GW. Its effects play on the Sound Blaster 16 (a SOUND.CFG of ours sets it up; the sound starts with your first click or key).

title: Wolfenstein 3D (shareware)
author: id Software, published by Apogee
blurb: Episode one, Escape from Wolfenstein, from Apogee's 1.4 shareware archive, unpacked in the browser as its installer would. Music and effects on the AdLib and Sound Blaster; the sound starts with your first click or key.

title: Commander Keen 1 (shareware)
author: id Software, published by Apogee
blurb: Marooned on Mars, the Apogee shareware episode of the Invasion of the Vorticons: id's smooth-scrolling EGA platformer, with PC speaker sound.

title: Commander Keen 4 (shareware)
author: id Software, published by Apogee
blurb: Secret of the Oracle, the Apogee shareware episode of Goodbye Galaxy: parallax EGA scrolling and AdLib music; the sound starts with your first click or key.

title: Fractint 20.0
author: The Stone Soup Group
blurb: The classic fractal generator. Enter for the menu, then F3 for VGA 256 colours: it draws the Mandelbrot set; zoom with Page Up and Enter.

title: Plasma
author: MIRAGE
blurb: A flowing plasma in VGA mode 13h, redrawn every frame, palette set through the DAC ports.

title: Munching squares
author: MIRAGE
blurb: x XOR y in mode 13h with a rotating palette, synchronised on the vertical retrace.

title: VESA banks
author: MIRAGE
blurb: Finds 640×480×256 by walking the VBE mode list, then draws through five bank switches.

title: EGA planes
author: MIRAGE
blurb: The EGA write modes, set/reset, bit mask and latches, in 16-colour planar mode 0Dh.

title: CGA palette
author: MIRAGE
blurb: CGA mode 4: four colour bars across the two interleaved banks.

title: Helium
author: viznut (ocsa)
blurb: A 4K intro from Assembly '97: a lonely planet, a story told in text, its own music player.

title: Puls
author: Řrřola
blurb: A raymarched lattice of spheres in 256 bytes (Riverwash 2009). It wants a fast machine: each frame takes a moment.

title: Difúze
author: Řrřola
blurb: Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion in 256 bytes (Riverwash 2010): sixteen rules, from a single line to cells, worms and spirals. Give it a minute to grow. Its music is General MIDI through an MPU-401, played by MIRAGE's own synthesizer.

title: Symetrie
author: Řrřola
blurb: A kaleidoscope of symmetric patterns, in 256 bytes.

title: Dírojed
author: Řrřola
blurb: “Hole eater”: an animated effect in 32 bytes.

title: Paralaxa
author: Řrřola
blurb: Parallax scrolling in 32 bytes, in the standard VGA palette.

title: TetrOS
author: Daniel Etzold
blurb: Tetris in a 512-byte boot sector. Arrow keys move, Up rotates.

title: Floppy Bird
author: Mihail Szabolcs
blurb: Flappy Bird as a bootable floppy, in 16-bit real mode. Space flaps.

title: BootChess
author: Olivier Poudade (Baudsurfer/RSi)
blurb: Chess against the computer in a 512-byte boot sector. Type a move such as e2e4 and press Enter.

title: bootRogue
author: Oscar Toledo G.
blurb: A roguelike in 510 bytes: random dungeons, monsters, the amulet. Arrow keys.

title: bootBASIC
author: Oscar Toledo G.
blurb: A BASIC interpreter in 512 bytes. Try: 10 print "hello" then run.

title: SectorLISP
author: Justine Tunney, Alain Greppin
blurb: A LISP with a garbage collector in a boot sector. Try: (CONS (QUOTE A) (QUOTE B))

title: sectorforth
author: Cesar Blum
blurb: A 16-bit Forth in 512 bytes: eight primitives (@ ! sp@ rp@ 0= + nand exit), and you define the rest. Try: : dup sp@ @ ;

title: FreeDOS 1.4
author: The FreeDOS Project
blurb: A whole DOS on a 64 MB hard disk, built from the FreeDOS project's own packages: EDIT, Bywater BASIC and FreeBASIC to write programs, Lua and NASM, and a few games (vitetris, Sudoku86, Liquid War, Kraptor, Floppy Bird). The menu is on screen.

title: The light
author: The Orz
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux, 1st at Outline 2023 (procedural graphics): a light on the horizon of a starry sea, made of AVX2 on YMM registers and drawn on /dev/fb0 at 1920x1080. It builds up over a minute.

title: Calculating Space
author: The Orz
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux, 2nd at Outline 2021: shards of light accumulating in AVX on /dev/fb0.

title: Campers
author: The Orz
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux, Outline 2021 (procedural graphics): a symmetric flame that builds up, in AVX and BMI2.

title: Apollonian
author: The Orz
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux, Shadow party 2021: an Apollonian gasket of glowing circles.

title: Flagship
author: The Orz
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux, Revision 2021 (wild): a ship of warm light, in C with AVX saturated arithmetic, on /dev/fb0 with two system calls.

title: QuasiSpace
author: The Orz
blurb: 128 bytes for Linux, Outline 2021: an ellipse in a foam of bubbles.

title: Mmrnmhrm
author: The Orz
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux, Lovebyte 2022: machinery in fire colours, in AVX2.

title: Crimson
author: The Orz
blurb: 128 bytes for Linux, Lovebyte 2022: grey planes sliding over each other.

title: Zeta
author: The Orz
blurb: 64 bytes for Linux, Lovebyte 2022: 64 bytes of code (and 50 of ELF header): coloured patterns seeded by where the stack lies.

title: Blin Elfom
author: Ye Olde Laptops Posse (w23, korvin)
license: no licence stated: fetched from its authors’ site
blurb: 197 bytes for Linux, Alternative Party 2011: a tiling of green and blue squares, and its own sound on /dev/dsp.

title: pattern
author: Ye Olde Laptops Posse (w23)
license: no licence stated: fetched from its authors’ site
blurb: 127 bytes for Linux, 2012: a shimmering pattern and its sound, from six bytes left after the setup.

title: attraction & decay
author: dominikr / Desire
license: no licence stated: fetched from its authors’ repository
blurb: 256 bytes for Linux (the party version, header not counted), Outline 2026: a Lorenz attractor drawn in the x87 FPU, double-buffered at 1920x1080, paced by a timerfd.
